prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and of its active form, which made incretin-based therapies for diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part B019 prize to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. After the full first-round exchange the case rests on the same points, and none of the six statements gave me a reason to doubt them. The chain from the incretin effect and proglucagon processing, through human GLP-1 physiology and the identification of the biologically active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, to receptor biology and then drugs with independently confirmed effects on glycaemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal outcomes is unusually complete. The field has changed in a way that is discernible and lasting. The evidence is mature and no member argues for delay. The chair's central question is whether the citation should reward physiology or physiology through to therapy. I think the prize is best given for the discovery, and that the discovery is the hormone, its active form and its actions. The therapy is the consequence that proves the discovery matters, and the citation can say so without crediting the drug-development step as a separate achievement.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weak point and I do not think round 2 has removed it. Three names cannot carry this history. Habener is outside the supplied list, and the committee has no primary-record evidence on his priority relative to Mojsov, so naming her takes a position we cannot fully verify from this material. Knudsen's acylated, albumin-binding analogues are what produced liraglutide and semaglutide, and a physiology-only citation under-credits that. I concede that this is a judgement and not a fact. I also concede that the physiology-first reading is partly a matter of how the committee has historically framed the prize. A two-part prize would not help: the three-person limit applies to the union of laureates, so adding B028 or B014 would force two of the three GLP-1 names out, and I would not make that trade. If diligence showed that Mojsov's contribution to the active peptide was not independent or not first, I would move to Drucker, Holst and Knudsen with a citation that includes therapy, and I would say that openly.

responses.point: Linnarsson holds Drucker, Holst and Knudsen for B019, argues that the step from a peptide with a half-life of minutes to a once-daily or once-weekly drug was a discovery in its own right, and says he would not block Mojsov under a purely physiological citation if her priority is discussed openly.
responses.response: I have taken your argument seriously and it has moved me on one point: I now regard the acylation and albumin-binding step as a real discovery, and I withdraw any suggestion that it is only industrial. It has not moved me on the choice of third name. A prize citing physiology and its therapeutic consequence needs the active hormone as its anchor, and the long-acting analogues presuppose the identification of GLP-1(7-36). You say priority against Habener cannot be adjudicated from the record. That applies equally to the Knudsen route, which would leave out both Mojsov and Habener and so omit two claimants instead of one. Since you would not block Mojsov in a physiology citation, I think we are closer than the five-to-one split suggests, and our real disagreement is about what the prize is for. I answer the chair's question by saying that the citation should name the active form and the therapeutic consequence, and that Knudsen is the first name I would change if the priority diligence goes against Mojsov.

responses.point: Per prefers Drucker, Holst and Mojsov with a citation built on the physiology and the active peptide, so that the prize stays in the discovery domain, while noting that a physiology-only prize can be read as under-crediting the step that created the drugs.
responses.response: I agree with the framing and with the three names, and I think your caution about blurring discovery and industrial optimisation is correct. I would add one qualification. A citation that stops at physiology and the active peptide, without mentioning the consequence, would read as incomplete given what the field has become. The wording we both seem to favour handles this, because it says the discoveries made the therapies possible without crediting the therapy itself. I disagree with one implication of your round-1 uncertainty. You raise B028 or B014 as a possible second part. I do not think a second part is warranted, because it would force a split of the GLP-1 names, and the strongest case on the list is stronger as a single prize than any pair we can build from it.

responses.point: Rickard supports Drucker, Holst and Mojsov because the prize then credits the scientific discovery and not industrial optimisation, ranks B028 as a fallback, and wonders whether a second part such as B028 would strengthen or dilute the prize.
responses.response: I agree with you that a second part risks diluting a prize that is already strong, and I would go further: given the union limit, it would subtract from B019 in order to add B028. Walter and Mori are a clean pair and I keep B028 as an alternative for that reason, but a clean pair is not a reason to weaken the lead case. I also note that you, like me, did not verify the Mojsov and Habener history from primary sources. That is a shared limitation and I would rather state it in the record than let the five of us treat the same unverified recollection as agreement. Where we differ slightly is in how we describe Knudsen. I no longer think 'credits discovery rather than industrial optimisation' is a safe description of her contribution, and I would keep the argument for excluding her on the ground of the three-person limit and the physiology framing, not on the nature of the work.

responses.point: Marie supports Drucker, Holst and Mojsov as a physiology-led prize, accepts that any trio omits someone with a real claim, and names B014 and B032 as mature, clearly attributable fallbacks if the committee judges the GLP-1 attribution too unstable.
responses.response: Your fallback logic is the most useful input on the chair's question about whether Habener's absence and the lack of primary-record verification justify deferral or a different configuration. My answer is that a documented caveat is enough, because the disagreement is about who completes the trio and not about whether the discovery is real or mature. I disagree that B014 is clearly attributable. Eshhar's earlier chimeric receptor concept is outside the credited names, and Rosenberg's place is not settled, so B014 has an attribution problem of its own, and I would not move to it merely to avoid the problem in B019. On B032 I remain where I was in round 1: the evidence is mature, but the discovery-level argument is weaker than for CAR-T, so I would not put it ahead of B014 as an alternative.

responses.point: Abdel supports Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, keeps B016 as his first alternative for its exceptional originality, and lists as an uncertainty whether the case should be deferred until a fuller review of priority is done.
responses.response: On deferral I disagree. The evidence is mature and the interpretation stable, and the open question is the third name, not the science. Deferring would leave the clearest case on the list unrewarded because of a credit dispute that a fuller review may never settle, while the committee's duty is to reach the best available judgement on the record it has. On B016 we agree that the scientific importance is not in doubt. My difficulty remains that six names compete for three places and that the channelrhodopsin discovery and its neuronal application are two achievements that a single trio would blend. I therefore keep it out of my alternatives, as in round 1, and I would need a configuration that separates those two steps before I could advance it.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1 peptide, relative to Habener's group, is secure; I cannot verify it from the supplied material.
Whether the committee will accept a citation that names the active form and the therapeutic consequence without crediting drug development, or whether it will insist on Knudsen.
How much weight Habener's absence from the supplied list should carry if no member can supply primary-record evidence.
If B019 were set aside, how to allocate credit within B014 among June, Sadelain and Rosenberg given Eshhar's omission.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict requiring recusal from B019, B014 or B028. I have co-authored nuclear-receptor work with Ronald Evans, who is not credited on any shortlisted candidate. My profile lists co-authored works with Per Svenningsson and one with Abdel El Manira, none involving a shortlisted candidate or credited name. These ties are unchanged since round 1.
